outline.description: Sets out the parties, core facts about Consilio’s overtime policy, the claims asserted under Minnesota wage statutes, the payments made, and how the case reached the Eighth Circuit on summary judgment.
subtopics: Parties and roles: Bruce Cohen (hourly licensed attorney reviewer) vs. Consilio, LLC (legal document review company)
2019 overtime policy change email: elimination of overtime premium; pay at base rate for all hours
Relief sought: overtime pay, liquidated damages, statutory penalties, injunctive relief
Consilio’s payments: $256,010.01 total; Cohen received $3,225.21 overtime + $462 liquidated damages; stipulation that all MFLSA overtime and liquidated damages are paid
Reserved dispute: availability of penalties under MPWA, MFLSA, MWTA
Procedural agreement: posture summary judgment first; if granted fully, case ends
District court ruling: summary judgment for Consilio on all claims; Cohen appeals

outline.description: Explains the Eighth Circuit’s de novo review of summary judgment and the standing/mootness principles that shape the MFLSA penalties issue.
subtopics: Summary judgment standard: no genuine dispute of material fact; entitlement to judgment as a matter of law
Viewing evidence in light most favorable to nonmovant
Standing must exist for each claim and form of relief (Town of Chester)
Continuing case-or-controversy requirement; mootness parallels standing (Sisney; Arizonans for Official English)
Civil penalties can deter ongoing violations and support redress (Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw)
Voluntary cessation and the ‘absolutely clear’ no-recurrence standard (Laidlaw; Concentrated Phosphate Exports)

outline.chapter_title: MPWA Claim: Who May Seek Average Daily Wage Penalties
outline.description: Analyzes whether employees can recover average daily wage penalties under MPWA § 181.101 via § 181.171, concluding that only the Commissioner may seek such penalties.
subtopics: Statutory framework: § 181.171 authorizes civil actions and ‘other appropriate relief’ for specified MPWA violations
Text of § 181.101(a): penalty authority vested in the Commissioner after serving a demand; monies collected paid to the employee
Employee right preserved: prosecute a claim for wages (not penalties) under § 181.101(a)
Plain-language canon and Minnesota cases (Allan; Milner): give effect to unambiguous text
Comparative statutes showing legislative choice to grant employees penalty rights elsewhere (§§ 181.13, 181.14; Lagasse; Hubbard ‘knows how’ inference)
Persuasive district authority: Hull v. ConvergeOne limiting penalty enforcement to the Commissioner
Holding: Employees cannot seek average daily wage penalties under § 181.101; summary judgment for Consilio affirmed on MPWA penalties

outline.chapter_title: MFLSA Penalties: Stipulations, Redressability, and Mootness Remand
outline.description: Addresses Cohen’s pursuit of statutory penalties under the MFLSA after being paid all overtime and liquidated damages, focusing on Article III issues and remand for jurisdictional determination.
subtopics: Stipulation: all MFLSA overtime and liquidated damages paid; only statutory penalties remain at issue
Parties’ agreement: penalties, if any, would be payable to the Commissioner, not Cohen
Redressability through civil penalties: potential to deter ongoing violations (Laidlaw)
Key factual uncertainty: whether Consilio’s allegedly unlawful overtime policy remains in effect
Mootness analysis: if policy ended and recurrence is ‘absolutely clear,’ claim may be moot; voluntary cessation doctrine
Disposition: vacatur of summary judgment on MFLSA claim; remand to determine jurisdiction (standing/mootness) before merits

outline.chapter_title: MWTA Claim and Injunctive Relief: Preservation and Statutory Limits
outline.description: Explains why the MWTA penalties claim fails and why injunctive relief was not considered, emphasizing preservation and proper pleading.
subtopics: MWTA theory: failure to provide required notice of overtime policy change (§ 181.032(f), (d)(4))
Stipulation: all owed pay received; absence of cited authority for civil penalties under MWTA in this posture
Waiver on appeal for undeveloped arguments (Milligan)
Injunctive relief: complaint sought specific relief; later request to rescind 2019 policy raised only in summary judgment briefing
Procedural rule: new claims or materially different injunctive theories must be raised by amended complaint (InfoDeli; Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a))
Holding: district court’s dismissal of MWTA and refusal to consider new injunctive request affirmed

outline.chapter_title: Disposition, Concurring Views, and Practical Takeaways
outline.description: Summarizes the judgment, notes the special concurrence, and highlights practice lessons for wage-and-hour litigation under Minnesota law.
subtopics: Judgment: MPWA and MWTA rulings affirmed; MFLSA ruling vacated and remanded for jurisdictional determination; injunctive relief not reached
Special concurrence (Judge Kobes): questions standing to seek MFLSA penalties under Laidlaw; suggests district court may resolve mootness first on remand
Practice pointers: plead precise injunctive relief early; understand Commissioner-only penalty schemes under MPWA § 181.101; preserve and brief statutory bases for penalties under MWTA
Strategic implications: payments and stipulations can shift disputes to Article III issues; ongoing-policy evidence critical to penalty claims grounded in deterrence
